William Congreve, The Way of the World.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/william-congreve/the-way-of-the-world

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- William Congreve, the author, died 1729 (Wikidata Q366805, P570 = 1729-01-19).
- Felix E. Schelling, the annotator, died 1945 (Wikidata Q5442196, Felix Emanuel Schelling, American academic, P570 = 1945-12-15; matched to the annotator named in the facts by name and description).

First publication of the text used: 1700 (SE colophon: 'The Way of the World was published in 1700 by William Congreve.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: Standard Ebooks states that the text is in the United States public domain (its rights statement is quoted below). The text was first published in 1700, before 1931, so it entered the United States public domain 95 years after publication, in 1795.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa, and each has a term of life plus 70 years or less for these deaths. The last person to die, Felix E. Schelling in 1945, makes the text public domain there from 1 January 2016. Nothing in the facts points to France, Spain, Mexico, Colombia or Russia/USSR, so the result is the same whichever of these countries it was first published in.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
